tells: 1. The back of the house is flat, uniform dark cut-out silhouettes standing in haze with no rim, no volume and no individual light falloff; they read as cardboard stand-ins, not people (club-1-wide.png, upper middle band behind the front tables; club-2-mid.png, upper left)

2. The laugh never arrives in the strip: across 1.0 s only heads turn and the white-shirt woman lifts a hand; no mouths open wide, no shoulders heave, no spread through the room, so nothing reads as caused by a line (club-5-strip.png, all six frames, front row)

3. The face close is game-character skin: waxy, poreless, evenly lit orange with a helmet hairline, plus a dark cut-out halo where the depth-of-field matte meets her white jacket (club-4-face.png, centre face and shoulder edges)

4. The front row is lit by an unmotivated soft frontal fill: faces are evenly bright from camera direction, while the only practical sources are tiny candles and wall sconces; the candles do not under-light chins or warm the faces (club-1-wide.png, front row faces centre; club-2-mid.png, faces at the tables)

5. Composition is stagy: everyone sits square-on to camera behind small tables in a single line, with nearly identical hands-on-table rest poses, like a lineup rather than a club seated around tables (club-1-wide.png, front row left to right; club-6-held.png, centre tables)

1. The wide is a flat, frontal, evenly exposed grid of upright mannequins: the back rows appear to stand bolt upright in a lattice with seats barely visible, no falloff with depth, and the stage spill lights every row equally (theatre-1-wide.png, whole upper two-thirds)

2. The face close shows a black, toothless, hole-like mouth interior and dead, unfocused eyes on a plastic, uniformly lit face; at TV distance it reads as a game NPC mid-scream rather than a laugh (theatre-4-face.png, centre face and mouth)

3. Flat black cut-out silhouettes fill the rear stalls and stack up into the haze, with no rims and identical tone, so the depth reads as a painted backdrop (theatre-2-mid.png and theatre-6-held.png, top third)

4. Posture: front-row people perch stiffly on the seat edge with knees together and hands clamped on thighs, and the same pose repeats across the row; several legs look thin and pressed, with feet planted identically (theatre-3-mid.png, front row centre-right; theatre-1-wide.png, front row)

5. Shading artefacts: a translucent red-glowing arm and torso on the left-row man, a blocky noisy hair or cap texture on the right-edge man, and dark matte outlines around the hoodie in the close (theatre-3-mid.png, left at x~180 and right edge; theatre-4-face.png, hoodie edges)
1. A face is visibly broken in a back-row man: a pale smeared blob where the nose and mouth should be (openmic-3-mid.png, centre behind the yellow shirt, around x~500 y~340)

2. Hair cards in the face close show stair-stepped, aliased edges at the back of the head, plus a dark cut-out halo where the depth-of-field matte meets the shoulder; the skin is waxy and evenly lit (openmic-4-face.png, right side of the head and shoulder line)

3. The wide is underexposed and muddy, with no key on faces; the row of evenly spaced wall downlights does not motivate the frontal fill on the crowd, and the dark-hoodie woman's legs glow pink-red like an emissive material (openmic-1-wide.png, crowd centre and lower centre legs)

4. Posture: almost everyone hunches forward with both hands on their knees in the same pose; in the held frame legs and knees interpenetrate between neighbouring seats and the line of chairs reads as a bench of mannequins (openmic-6-held.png, lower centre legs; openmic-1-wide.png, front row)

5. In the laugh strip only two or three people react (the green-shirt and hoodie women open their mouths and turn); the yellow-shirt man and the left side stay frozen, and the reaction reads as chatting to a neighbour rather than laughing at the stage (openmic-5-strip.png, frames t=12.6 to 13.0, centre-right)
